commit.message:
bug #5039 Fix a variable not being escaped when it has the name of a macro import alias of another scope (jack-worman)

This PR was squashed before being merged into the 3.x branch.

Discussion
----------

Fix a variable not being escaped when it has the name of a macro import alias of another scope

The escaper treats `x.attr`, `x['key']` and `x.method()` as safe whenever `{% import … as x %}` appears anywhere in the template. That rule (8832b660b) dates from when macro calls compiled to attribute reads on the alias. Since 3.0 they compile to macro references (`MacroReferenceExpression` today), which are already safe, so the rule only matches ordinary variables that share the alias name in another block or macro, and prints them unescaped:

```twig
{% block header %}{% import _self as item %}{{ item.hello() }}{% endblock %}
{% block content %}{% for item in items %}{{ item.body }}{% endfor %}{% endblock %}
```

`item.body` is output raw. The same happens with an import in one macro and an argument of that name in a later macro, and with a top-level import placed after the block that uses the name.

This removes the rule. Macro calls through an alias stay safe through `MacroReferenceExpression`, and `attribute(alias, 'name')` can't reach macros, since aliases live in `$macros`, not in the context.
